classic.description: The sound of cutting a solid material such as wood into smaller pieces by using an ax or other hacking tool.

classic.name: Splinter
classic.description: The sound of a rigid fibrous material, typically wood, breaking up into splinters or slivers.

classic.name: Crack
classic.description: Abrupt sounds of individual ruptures in a rigid substance under stress.

classic.name: Glass
classic.description: Sounds associated with the non-crystalline amorphous solid that is often transparent and has widespread practical, technological, and decorative uses.

classic.name: Chink, clink
classic.description: A short light metallic sound.

classic.name: Shatter
classic.description: The sound of a brittle rigid substance rapidly breaking into many pieces.

classic.name: Liquid
classic.description: Sounds of a fluid that conforms to the shape of its container but retains a constant volume independent of pressure.

classic.name: Splash, splatter
classic.description: The sound of a liquid colliding with a hard surface.

classic.name: Slosh
classic.description: The sound of small waves of liquid held in a container breaking against the edges.

classic.name: Squish
classic.description: Sounds made by a liquid-saturated material being squeezed.

classic.name: Drip
classic.description: The sound of liquid falling in drops.

classic.name: Pour
classic.description: The sound of liquid being transferred in a steady stream.

classic.name: Trickle, dribble
classic.description: The sound of a liquid flowing slowly in an unsteady stream or drops.

classic.name: Gush
classic.description: The sound of a liquid coming out of a pipe or other opening rapidly and in large volumes.

classic.name: Fill (with liquid)
classic.description: The sound of a container being filled with liquid.

classic.name: Spray
classic.description: The sound of a liquid being transferred in a scatter or jet of droplets.

classic.name: Pump (liquid)
classic.description: The sound of a liquid being drawn or poured with a pump.

classic.name: Stir
classic.description: The sound of moving an implement through a fluid substance.

classic.name: Boiling
classic.description: The sound of a liquid that is reaching the temperature at which it transitions to a vapor, resulting in bubbles emerging at the surface.

classic.name: Sonar
classic.description: Sounds associated with underwater sensing via acoustic signals. A classic sonar sound involves reverberant reflections of an emitted tone pip.

classic.name: Arrow
classic.description: Sounds of a shafted projectile that is shot with a bow.

classic.name: Whoosh, swoosh, swish
classic.description: A sibilant sound caused by a rigid object sweeping through the air.

classic.name: Thump, thud
classic.description: A heavy dull sound, as made by impact of heavy objects with a relatively soft point of contact.

classic.name: Thunk
classic.description: A partly dull hollow sound with a damped resonance.

classic.name: Electronic tuner
classic.description: Sounds produced by an electronic device whose purpose is to aid in the tuning of musical instruments.

classic.name: Effects unit
classic.description: Sounds associated with an electronic device that alters how a musical instrument or other audio source sounds. Some effects subtly "color" a sound while others transform it dramatically.

classic.name: Chorus effect
classic.description: The ensemble sound produced by an electronic effects unit which outputs simultaneous versions of the input source with small variations in pitch and timbre.

classic.name: Basketball bounce
classic.description: The sound of a basketball bouncing on a hard surface, such as a basketball court.

classic.name: Bang
classic.description: A brief and loud noise.

classic.name: Slap, smack
classic.description: The sharp sound of a flat object striking another (e.g., an open hand hitting a face).

classic.name: Whack, thwack
classic.description: The sound of a partially rigid object forcefully striking another object, which may be preceded by the sound of the rapid, driven motion of one object (as of a baseball bat hitting a ball).

classic.name: Smash, crash
classic.description: The sound of a rigid structure violently breaking into many pieces.

classic.name: Breaking
classic.description: The sound of a rigid object become separated into pieces or fragments.

classic.name: Bouncing
classic.description: The sound of an elastic, non-destructive collision in which one or both objects spring back. Depending on the situation, there may be multiple such collisions in a characteristic pattern, as of a ball bouncing.

classic.name: Whip
classic.description: The sound of whipping, i.e., the greatly accelerated motion of the tip of a flexible structure, as the result of concentrated angular momentum.

classic.name: Flap
classic.description: The noisy sound of a flexible surface, such as a flag, moving back-and-forth in the air and optionally coming into contact with an adjacent hard surface.

classic.name: Scratch
classic.description: The sound of a hard, sharp point of contact leaving a permanent groove in a hard surface.

classic.name: Scrape
classic.description: The sound of a hard edge dragging across a surface.

classic.name: Rub
classic.description: The sound of two surfaces moving smoothly over each other with pressure but without excessive friction.

classic.name: Roll
classic.description: The sound of an object moving by turning over or rotating.

classic.name: Crushing
classic.description: The sound of a brittle, rigid structure breaking into small pieces or catastrophically deforming.

classic.name: Crumpling, crinkling
classic.description: The sound of a rigid but flexible sheet, such as paper or aluminum, buckling into a smaller volume.

classic.name: Tearing
classic.description: The sound of a flat or smooth surface separating abruptly.

classic.name: Beep, bleep
classic.description: A short, single tone, generally made by a computer or other machine and typically high-pitched.

classic.name: Ping
classic.description: A sharp high-pitched resonant sound with a clear decay.

classic.name: Ding
classic.description: A high-pitched ringing sound, as of a small metal object being struck.

classic.name: Clang
classic.description: A loud, resonant, discordant noise, as of a large and partly hollow metal structure begin struck.

classic.name: Squeal
classic.description: A short, high-pitched tone without a sharp attack and with a perceptible variation in pitch.

classic.name: Creak
classic.description: A high-pitched noise with a perceptible variation in pitch as a result of pressure being shifted or applied on a surface, most commonly on wood.

classic.name: Rustle
classic.description: A sound of light, thin objects, such as dried leaves, rubbing against one another.

classic.name: Whir
classic.description: A quiet sound of a small object, typically mechanical, in rapid, cyclic motion.

classic.name: Clatter
classic.description: An irregular rattling noise, often produced by rapid movement, consisting of a cluster of transient sounds.

classic.name: Sizzle
classic.description: The sound of many small bubbles bursting, most often caused by fat vaporizing as it is heated.

classic.name: Clicking
classic.description: A short, pitchless, transient sound, as of a gentle impact between small hard objects.

classic.name: Clickety-clack
classic.description: The sound of fast and rhythmic clicking of machinery, such as keystrokes on a typewriter or steel wheels running on tracks.  Does not include the sound of horses feet (use /m/07rv9rh).

classic.name: Rumble
classic.description: A loud, low-pitched, dull, continuous noise.

classic.name: Plop
classic.description: The sound of a small object dropping into a liquid without a splash.

classic.name: Jingle, tinkle
classic.description: An irregular pattern of short metallic sounds, especially from small metal objects such as keys or coins shaking against each other.

classic.name: Hum
classic.description: A continuous, dull tone.

classic.name: Zing
classic.description: A brief high-pitched buzzing or humming sound.

classic.name: Boing
classic.description: A bouncing or spring-like sound with a tonal component that sweeps upwards.

classic.name: Crunch
classic.description: The sound of a brittle substance being crushed.

classic.name: Silence
classic.description: The absence of audible sound or presence of sounds of very low intensity.

classic.name: Sine wave
classic.description: A continuous, pure tone of fixed pitch and amplitude.

classic.name: Harmonic
classic.description: A sine tone whose frequency is an integer multiple of some fundamental tone.

classic.name: Chirp tone
classic.description: A tone whose frequency increases or decreases with time.

classic.name: Sound effect
classic.description: An artificially created or enhanced sound used to emphasize artistic or other content of films, television shows, live performances, animation, video games, music, or other media.

classic.name: Pulse
classic.description: A sound that is modulated in short, regular bursts at approximately 1 Hz.  This class is not for heartbeat sounds, use /m/01jg02.

classic.name: Inside, small room
classic.description: Sounds that appear to have been recorded within a small room, such as one that can accommodate no more than 15 people.

classic.name: Inside, large room or hall
classic.description: Sounds that appear to have been recorded in a large room or hall, often with clearly perceptible reverberation.

classic.name: Inside, public space
classic.description: Sounds that appear to have been recorded in a public space such as store, restaurant, or travel terminus, often characterized by both reverberation and continuous background noise.

classic.name: Outside, urban or manmade
classic.description: Sounds that appear to have been recorded outdoors in a human-constructed environment.

classic.name: Outside, rural or natural
classic.description: Sounds that appear to have been recorded outdoors in a natural, non-manmade environment.

classic.name: Reverberation
classic.description: The sound of an acoustic environment that includes substantial reflection from multiple walls or other hard surfaces. Reverberation is generally perceived as being able to 'hear' the presence and size of the room or space in which the sound is made.  The reflected sounds should remain audible for hundreds of milliseconds or longer.

classic.name: Echo
classic.description: A sound which is a delayed and attenuated repetition of an earlier sound, for example because the sound wave has been reflected back from a distant, planar surface. To be perceived as an echo, the repetion must be delayed by around 100 milliseconds or more.

classic.name: Noise
classic.description: A sound that has no perceptible structure and that typically interferes with the perception of more interesting or important sounds.

classic.name: Environmental noise
classic.description: The combined sounds of transport, industrial, and recreational activities.

classic.name: Static
classic.description: A crackling or hissing noise caused by electrical interference.

classic.name: Mains hum
classic.description: A low, continuous tone caused by electromagnetic interference from the alternating current of the mains electricity. The fundamental frequency of this sound is usually 50 Hz or 60 Hz, depending on the local power-line frequency.

classic.name: Distortion
classic.description: A sound that has been modified in a nonlinear fashion, usually in electronic equipment, to introduce sound correlated with the original signal. In many cases, notably with amplified electric musical instruments, distortion is introduced as an effect by increasing the gain and clipping the source signal.

classic.name: Sidetone
classic.description: The audible feedback on a telecommunications channel that allows the speaker to know that the channel is operational.

classic.name: Cacophony
classic.description: A loud, confusing, disagreeable sound, such as many voices shouting simultaneously.

classic.name: White noise
classic.description: A random, unstructured sound in which the value at any moment provides no information about the value at any other moment. White noise has equal energy in all frequency bands.

classic.name: Pink noise
classic.description: Unstructured noise whose energy decreases with frequency such that equal amounts of energy are distributed in logarithmic bands of frequency, typically octaves.  Pink noise sounds more like a rumble where white noise sounds like a hiss.

classic.name: Throbbing
classic.description: A dull, continunous sound with a strong rhythmic modulation.

classic.name: Vibration
classic.description: The general class of sounds caused by a periodic mechanical oscillation.

classic.name: Television
classic.description: A sound that appears to have been produced by a television set.

classic.name: Radio
classic.description: A sound that appears to have been produced by a radio receiver.

classic.name: Field recording
classic.description: A sound that appears to have been recorded in some specific environment, usually with the intention of capturing and representing that environment.

strong.name: Kettle whistle
strong.description: The high-pitched sound of a whistle attached to the spout of an appliance for boiling water.  When the water boils, steam is forced through the whistle, alerting users that boiling is complete.

strong.name: Firecracker
strong.description: The sound of a small explosive device primarily designed to produce a large amount of noise, especially in the form of a loud bang.

strong.name: Wild animals
strong.description: Sounds associated with animals not normally raised by humans.

strong.name: Motor vehicle (road)
strong.description: Sounds of self-propelled land vehicles, usually wheeled, that do not operate on rails. Includes "off-road" vehicles designed for unmade roads.

strong.name: Ambulance (siren)
strong.description: The sound of a siren fitted to a vehicle used to transport sick or injured people to a hospital or other medical facility.

strong.name: Fire engine, fire truck (siren)
strong.description: The sound of a siren fitted to a vehicle used to transport firefighters and their equipment to an emergency situation.

strong.name: Toothbrush
strong.description: Sounds of an instrument used to clean the teeth and gums consisting of a head of tightly clustered bristles mounted on a handle.

strong.name: Sink (filling or washing)
strong.description: Sounds originating from a bowl-shaped plumbing fixture that stores and drains water and that is used for washing hands, dishwashing, and other purposes.

strong.name: Aircraft engine
strong.description: The sound of the part of an aircraft that generates mechanical power. Aircraft engines are almost always lightweight piston engines, gas turbines, or, in small multicopter UAVs, electric motors.

strong.name: Explosion
strong.description: The sound of a rapid increase in volume and release of energy in an extreme manner, usually with the generation of high temperatures and the release of gases.

strong.name: Change ringing (campanology)
strong.description: Sounds of the art of ringing a set of (typically large) tuned bells in a controlled manner to produce variations in their sounding order.

strong.name: Dial tone
strong.description: The sound of a signal that a telephone exchange or other switching equipment sends to a telephone to confirm that it is ready to initiate a connection.

strong.name: Singing
strong.description: Musical sounds produced with the human voice, including sustained tonality, rhythm, and a variety of other vocal techniques.

strong.name: Bird
strong.description: Sounds associated with the large group of flying vertebrates.

strong.name: Digestive
strong.description: Sounds associated with the human function of eating and processing nutrition (food).

strong.name: Basketball bounce
strong.description: The sound of a basketball bouncing on a hard surface, such as a basketball court.

strong.name: Sonic boom
strong.description: The sound associated with the shock waves created by an object traveling through the air faster than the speed of sound.

strong.name: Subway, metro, underground
strong.description: Sounds of high-capacity electric railways that serve as public transport, generally in urban areas.

strong.name: Bicycle, tricycle
strong.description: Sounds of a human-powered, pedal-driven vehicle, having two wheels attached to a frame, one behind the other.

strong.name: Boat, Water vehicle
strong.description: Sounds of watercraft designed to float, plane, work, or travel on water.

strong.name: Sawing
strong.description: Sounds of a tool consisting of a tough blade, wire, or chain with a hard toothed edge, used to cut through material, most often wood.  Includes both manual and motorized saws.

strong.name: Reverberation
strong.description: The sound of an acoustic environment that includes substantial reflection from multiple walls or other hard surfaces. Reverberation is generally perceived as being able to 'hear' the presence and size of the room or space in which the sound is made.  The reflected sounds should remain audible for hundreds of milliseconds or longer.

strong.name: Cough
strong.description: A sudden and often repetitively occurring reflex which consists of an inhalation, a forced exhalation against a closed glottis, and a violent release of air following opening of the glottis.

strong.name: Bus
strong.description: Interior and exterior sounds of a road vehicle designed to carry many passengers.

strong.name: Mantra
strong.description: A melodic sacred utterance believed to have spiritual powers.

strong.name: Drill
strong.description: Sounds of a tool used for making holes in various materials via a rotating drill bit.

strong.name: Snoring
strong.description: The sound resulting from obstructed respiratory airways during breathing while sleeping.

strong.name: Gull, seagull
strong.description: Sounds associated with the family of seabirds often encountered in coastal regions.

strong.name: Railroad car, train wagon
strong.description: The sound of a vehicle used for carrying cargo or passengers on a rail transport system.

strong.name: Stomach rumble
strong.description: A rumbling, growling or gurgling noise produced by movement of the contents of the gastro-intestinal tract.

strong.name: Bee, wasp, etc.
strong.description: Sounds associated with these closely-related species of flying insects known for pollination, honey-production, and the ability to sting humans.

strong.name: Engine knocking
strong.description: A metallic "pinging" sound caused by a malfunctioning spark-ignited internal combustion engine. Engine knocking indicates that the combustion of the air/fuel mixture in the cylinder is occurring at the wrong point in the piston's stroke.

strong.name: Conversation
strong.description: Interactive, spontaneous spoken communication between two or more people.

strong.name: Yak
strong.description: The sound of the long-haired bovid found throughout the Himalaya region of southern Central Asia.

strong.name: Ringtone
strong.description: The synthesized or pre-recorded sounds made by contemporary electronic telephones to indicate an incoming call or text message.

strong.name: Sneeze
strong.description: A convulsive expulsion of air from the lungs through the nose and mouth, usually caused by foreign particles irritating the nasal mucous.

strong.name: Laughter
strong.description: The sound of rhythmical contractions of the diaphragm in response to stimuli such as tickling, or from humorous stories or thoughts.

strong.name: Yawn
strong.description: The sound of a reflex consisting of the simultaneous inhalation of air and the stretching of the eardrums, followed by an exhalation of breath, commonly associated with tiredness. Specifically refers to humans.

strong.name: Chainsaw
strong.description: The sound of a portable mechanical saw which cuts with a set of teeth attached to a rotating chain. Chainsaws are commonly powered by a small two-stroke internal combustion engine.

strong.name: Heart sounds, heartbeat
strong.description: Noises generated by the beating heart and the resultant flow of blood through it.

strong.name: Heart murmur
strong.description: Heart sounds produced by abnormal blood flow across one of the heart valves, typically detected by a stethoscope.

strong.name: Echo
strong.description: A sound which is a delayed and attenuated repetition of an earlier sound, for example because the sound wave has been reflected back from a distant, planar surface. To be perceived as an echo, the repetion must be delayed by around 100 milliseconds or more.

strong.name: Toilet flush
strong.description: The sound of a toilet flushing water along with any waste through a drainpipe.

strong.name: Vibration
strong.description: The general class of sounds caused by a periodic mechanical oscillation.

strong.name: Scissors
strong.description: The sound of hand-operated shearing tools consisting of a pair of metal blades pivoted so that the sharpened edges slide against each other when the handles opposite to the pivot are closed.

strong.name: Computer keyboard
strong.description: Sounds created by a typewriter-style device which uses an arrangement of buttons or keys controlling switches to enter text or other information into a computer or other electronic device.

strong.name: Printer
strong.description: Sounds of a computer peripheral which makes a persistent human readable representation of graphics or text on paper or similar physical media.

strong.name: Turkey
strong.description: Sounds associated with the large poultry bird, originally domesticated in the Americas.

strong.name: Zipper (clothing)
strong.description: The sound of a device consisting of two rows of small interlocking teeth for binding the edges of an opening of fabric or other flexible material, like on a garment or a bag.

strong.name: Cellphone buzz, vibrating alert
strong.description: The low buzz emitted by the vibrotactile actuator used to provide "silent alarms" on mobile phones and other devices.

strong.name: Yodeling
strong.description: A form of singing that involves repeated and rapid changes of pitch between the low-pitch chest register and the high-pitch head register or falsetto.

strong.name: Sine wave
strong.description: A continuous, pure tone of fixed pitch and amplitude.

strong.name: Whistling
strong.description: High-pitched tone produced by blowing or sucking air through a small opening between the lips. Used to draw attention, as a personal tic, and to reproduce a melody.

strong.name: Clock
strong.description: Sounds made by an instrument designed to keep and indicate time.

strong.name: Cattle, bovinae
strong.description: Sounds associated with the most common type of large domesticated ungulates.

strong.name: Smoke detector, smoke alarm
strong.description: Sounds emitted by a device that senses smoke, typically to warn of a fire.

strong.name: Lawn mower
strong.description: The sound of a machine utilizing one or more revolving blades to cut grass, powered by an electric motor, a small internal combustion engine, or by a human pushing the machine.

strong.name: Cat
strong.description: Sounds associated with the familiar, furry, domestic carnivorous mammal.

strong.name: Busy signal
strong.description: A sound (usually a simple repeating tone) played over a telephone line to indicate that the requested connection could not be completed, for instance because the remote party is already engaged in a different call.

strong.name: Canidae, wild dogs, wolves
strong.description: Sounds associated with the wild relatives of domesticated dogs.

strong.name: Chipmunk
strong.description: Sounds associated with the small, striped rodents of the family Sciuridae.

strong.name: Bird vocalization, bird call, bird song
strong.description: Bird communication calls, often considered melodious to the human ear.

strong.name: Cowbell
strong.description: A simple metal bell historically tied around the necks of cattle to keep track of their whereabouts.

strong.name: Cutlery, silverware
strong.description: The sounds of hand implements such as knife, fork, and spoon, that are typically made of steel and are used in preparing, serving, and eating food in the Western world.

strong.name: Sanding
strong.description: The sounds of a surface being scraped by an abrasive material affixed to sheets of paper or cloth, either to make the surface smoother, remove a layer of material, or sometimes to make the surface rougher.

strong.name: Coin (dropping)
strong.description: The sound of a small, flat, round piece of hard material such as metal or plastic colliding with or bouncing on a hard surface.

strong.name: Cash register
strong.description: Sounds of a mechanical or electronic device for registering and calculating transactions, usually attached to a drawer for storing cash.

strong.name: Finger snapping
strong.description: A snapping or clicking sound usually caused by building tension between the thumb and another finger and then moving the other finger forcefully downward to hits the palm at high speed.

strong.name: Fowl
strong.description: Sounds associated with the bird species commonly raised for human consumption.

strong.name: Air conditioning
strong.description: The sound of a device that removes heat from the air inside a building or vehicle, thus lowering the air temperature.

strong.name: Babbling
strong.description: Speech-like sounds uttered by a human that lack the deeper structure and meaning of conventional speech. Babbling is a stage in a child's development of language.

strong.name: Wind chime
strong.description: The sound of an instrument constructed from suspended tubes, rods, bells, or other objects that are often made of metal or wood along with some type of weight the tubes or rods can strike when they or another wind-catching surface are blown by the natural movement of air outside.

strong.name: Jingle bell
strong.description: The sound of a type of bell which produces a distinctive 'jingle' sound, especially in large numbers. They are commonly produced from a single piece of sheet metal bent into a roughly spherical shape containing a small ball bearing.

strong.name: Train horn
strong.description: The sound of an air horn which serves as an audible warning device on diesel and electric locomotives.

strong.name: Applause
strong.description: Group expression of approval by the collective act of clapping by a group.

strong.name: Silence
strong.description: The absence of audible sound or presence of sounds of very low intensity.

strong.name: Fire
strong.description: Sounds resulting from  the rapid oxidation of a material in the exothermic chemical process of combustion, releasing heat, light, and various reaction products.

strong.name: Fart
strong.description: The release of gasses produced by digestion through the anus; flatulence.

strong.name: Chant
strong.description: The rhythmic speaking or singing of words or sounds, often primarily on one or two main pitches called reciting tones.

strong.name: Ratchet, pawl
strong.description: The sound of a mechanical device that allows continuous linear or rotary motion in only one direction while preventing motion in the opposite direction.

strong.name: Telephone dialing, DTMF
strong.description: The sound of a telephony signaling system where short combinations of tones within the frequency range of human speech are used to transmit individual digits.

strong.name: Door
strong.description: Sounds of a moving structure used to open or close an entrance to an enclosed space such as a building or vehicle.

strong.name: Beep, bleep
strong.description: A short, single tone, generally made by a computer or other machine and typically high-pitched.

strong.name: Humming
strong.description: A wordless tone produced by forcing the sound to emerge from the nose, often with a melody.

strong.name: Electric shaver, electric razor
strong.description: The sound of a bladed tool primarily used in the removal of unwanted body hair where the blades are continually moved by an electric motor.

strong.name: Water tap, faucet
strong.description: The sound of a hand-operated valve controlling the release of water, for instance as fitted to a sink or bath, and the resulting water flow.

strong.name: Propeller, airscrew
strong.description: The sound of an aircraft propulsion system that converts rotary motion from an engine via a rotating set of blades into forward thrust through the air.

strong.name: Car alarm
strong.description: The loud sound of an electronic device installed in a vehicle in an attempt to discourage theft of the vehicle or its contents.

strong.name: Engine
strong.description: The sound of a machine designed to produce mechanical energy. Combustion engines burn a fuel to create heat, which then creates a force. Electric motors convert electrical energy into mechanical motion. Other classes of engines include pneumatic motors and clockwork motors.

strong.name: Filing (rasp)
strong.description: Sounds of a common wood- and metal-working tool used to remove fine amounts of material from a workpiece.

strong.name: Hiccup
strong.description: A strong, involuntary contraction of the diaphragm that may repeat several times per minute.

strong.name: Blender, food processor
strong.description: The sound of a kitchen and laboratory appliance used to mix, purée, or emulsify food and other substances, usually by means of metal blades at the base of a container spun rapidly by an electric motor.

strong.name: Narration, monologue
strong.description: Speech by a single human aimed at an audience (either present or assumed, as in a video blog).

strong.name: Reversing beeps
strong.description: The sound of an electronic warning device fitted to many commercial vehicles to alert pedestrians when the reverse gear is engaged, signaling that the vehicle is likely to move backwards.

strong.name: Motorboat, speedboat
strong.description: Sounds of a boat which is powered by an inboard or outboard engine.

strong.name: Effects unit
strong.description: Sounds associated with an electronic device that alters how a musical instrument or other audio source sounds. Some effects subtly "color" a sound while others transform it dramatically.

strong.name: Whispering
strong.description: Unvoiced speech, usually intended to be quieter to avoid causing disturbance or being overheard.

strong.name: Mechanical fan
strong.description: Sounds of a machine used to create air flow via the motion of a rotating arrangement of vanes or blades.

strong.name: Sliding door
strong.description: The sound of a type of door which opens horizontally by sliding, usually parallel to a wall.

strong.name: Purr
strong.description: A tonal fluttering sound made by cats to indicate contentment or relaxed pleasure.

strong.name: Fusillade
strong.description: The sound of the simultaneous and continuous firing of a group of firearms on command.

strong.name: Female speech, woman speaking
strong.description: Speech uttered by an adult female human.

strong.name: Buzzer
strong.description: Sounds of a mechanical, electromechanical, or piezoelectric signaling device that emits a steady, highly-audible tone with a spectrum extending to high frequencies.

strong.name: Typing
strong.description: The sound of writing or inputting text by pressing keys on a typewriter, computer keyboard, cell phone, or calculator.

strong.name: Whale vocalization
strong.description: Sounds produced by whales for different kinds of communication.

strong.name: Gunshot, gunfire
strong.description: The sound of the discharge of a firearm, or multiple such discharges.

strong.name: Waves, surf
strong.description: Sounds caused by the surface waves that occur on the free surface of oceans, seas, lakes, rivers, etc., resulting from the wind blowing over the surface.

strong.name: Bell
strong.description: The sound of a simple instrument usually consisting of metal cast in the shape of a hollow cup, whose sides form a resonator which vibrates in a single tone upon being struck by a "clapper" suspended within, or by a separate mallet or hammer.

strong.name: Glass
strong.description: Sounds associated with the non-crystalline amorphous solid that is often transparent and has widespread practical, technological, and decorative uses.

strong.name: Chewing, mastication
strong.description: Food being crushed and ground by teeth.

strong.name: Ice cream truck, ice cream van
strong.description: Sounds of a commercial vehicle that serves as a mobile retail outlet for ice cream, usually during the summer. Ice cream vans often play a repeating nursery-rhyme-style melody from speakers mounted on the vehicle's exterior to attract customers.

strong.name: Bathtub (filling or washing)
strong.description: Sounds originating from a large container for holding water in which a person may bathe.

strong.name: Goat
strong.description: Sounds of the medium-sized domesticated bovidae.

strong.name: Emergency vehicle
strong.description: The sound of any vehicle that is designated and authorized to respond to an emergency. Since emergency vehicles often need to travel at high speeds, they are frequently fitted with audible sirens to warn other motorists to give way.

strong.name: Horse
strong.description: Sounds associated with the familiar domesticated large, fast, and strong ungulate mammal.

strong.name: Siren
strong.description: The sound of a loud noise-making device used to provide warnings to people nearby. A siren typically consists of a single pitch that changes either smoothly or abruptly on timescales around one second.

strong.name: Hammer
strong.description: Sounds made by a tool or device that delivers a blow to an object. Most hammers are hand tools used to drive nails, fit parts, forge metal, and break apart objects.

strong.name: Wind
strong.description: Sounds caused by the large-scale flow of gases, especially the air flowing over the surface of the Earth. Long-duration winds have various names associated with their average strength, such as breeze, gale, storm, and hurricane.

strong.name: Jackhammer
strong.description: The sound of a pneumatic or electro-mechanical tool that combines a hammer directly with a chisel, usually used to break up rock, pavement, and concrete.

strong.name: Burping, eructation
strong.description: The release of gas from the digestive tract through the mouth.

strong.name: Screaming
strong.description: A sharp, high-pitched human vocalization; often an instinctive action indicating fear, pain, surprise, joy, anger, etc. Verbal content is absent or overwhelmed, unlike Shout and Yell.

strong.name: Crowd
strong.description: The sound of a large group of people gathered together.

strong.name: Keys jangling
strong.description: Sounds made by the mutual collision of small pieces of metal, which are often linked on a ring, used to operate locks.

strong.name: Insect
strong.description: Sounds associated with invertebrates from the arthropod phylum that have a chitinous exoskeleton, a three-part body, three pairs of jointed legs, compound eyes, and one pair of antennae.

strong.name: Church bell
strong.description: The sound of a large bell usually encountered in churches where it used either to signify the hour or the time for worshippers to go to church.

strong.name: Hair dryer
strong.description: The sound of an electromechanical device designed to blow normal or hot air over damp hair, in order to dry the hair.

strong.name: Doorbell
strong.description: The sound of a signaling device typically placed near a building's entrance with which a visitor can announce their presence to occupants.

strong.name: Duck call (hunting tool)
strong.description: The sound of a tool which imitates the communication calls of waterfowl and is used primarily by hunters to lure prey.

strong.name: Jet engine
strong.description: The sound of an internal combustion airbreathing engine that generates thrust by discharging a fast-moving jet of gas. Jet aircraft use such engines for long-distance travel.

strong.name: Crying, sobbing
strong.description: Sound associated with the shedding of tears in response to an emotional state, arising from slow but erratic inhalation, occasional instances of breath holding and muscular tremor.

strong.name: Alarm clock
strong.description: Sounds made by a clock that is designed to make an audible signal at a specific time. The primary use of alarm clocks is to awaken people from their night's sleep.

strong.name: Motorcycle
strong.description: Sounds of a small motor vehicle, usually with only two wheels. Motorcycles typically lack an external shell and seat riders astride the engine.

strong.name: Dishes, pots, and pans
strong.description: The sound of non-destructive collisions between plates, dishes, glassware, cooking vessels, and kitchen and eating utensils.

strong.name: Roar
strong.description: A deep, bellowing outburst of sound forced through an open mouth, made by a lion or other "big cat" species.

strong.name: Electric toothbrush
strong.description: The sound of a toothbrush that makes rapid, automatic bristle motions driven by an electric motor in order to clean teeth.

strong.name: Foghorn
strong.description: A signaling sound used primarily in foggy conditions to warn watercraft of the presence of nearby vessels or other navigational hazards.

strong.name: Power windows, electric windows
strong.description: The sound of automobile windows being raised and lowered by a built-in electric motor, controlled by a button or switch.

strong.name: Battle cry
strong.description: A yell or chant taken up in battle, usually by members of the same combatant group, aiming at arousing aggression on one's own side and intimidating the enemy.

strong.name: Liquid
strong.description: Sounds of a fluid that conforms to the shape of its container but retains a constant volume independent of pressure.

strong.name: Police car (siren)
strong.description: The sound of a siren fitted to a ground vehicle used by police when responding to incidents.

strong.name: Music
strong.description: Music is an art form and cultural activity whose medium is sound and silence. The common elements of music are pitch, rhythm, dynamics, and the sonic qualities of timbre and texture.

strong.name: Mouse
strong.description: Sounds associated with the familiar small rodent.

strong.name: Crow
strong.description: Sounds associated with the species of medium-to-large birds, Corvus.

strong.name: Booing
strong.description: Vocal display of displeasure for someone or something, generally an entertainer, by loudly yelling "boo!" or making other noises of disparagement.

strong.name: Machine gun
strong.description: Sounds of a fully automatic mounted or portable firearm, designed to fire bullets in quick succession from an ammunition belt or magazine, typically at a rate of 300 to 1800 rounds per minute.

strong.name: Train whistle
strong.description: The sound of an audible signaling device on a steam locomotive used to warn that the train is approaching, and to communicate with rail workers.

strong.name: Cheering
strong.description: Encouraging, stimulating, or exciting vocalizations indicating approval or welcoming persons, announcements, etc.

strong.name: Rowboat, canoe, kayak
strong.description: Sounds of a boat propelled using the motion of oars in the water.

strong.name: Bird flight, flapping wings
strong.description: Sounds caused by a bird's use of its wings to travel through the air.

strong.name: Ocean
strong.description: Sounds of the body of saline water that composes much of Earth's surface.

strong.name: Packing tape, duct tape
strong.description: Sounds associated with self-adhesive tape from wide rolls used to seal cardboard boxes and other temporary attachments. Specifically includes the distinctive noise of the tape being dispensed from a roll.

strong.name: Shuffling cards
strong.description: The sound of playing cards being manually rearranged into a random order.

strong.name: Bark
strong.description: Principal communication sound produced by dogs. Often transliterated as woof, especially for large dogs.

strong.name: Air horn, truck horn
strong.description: The sound of a pneumatic device mounted on large vehicles designed to create an extremely loud noise for signalling purposes.

strong.name: Pulleys
strong.description: Sounds of a wheel on an axle or shaft that is designed to support movement and change of direction of a taut cable or belt along its circumference.

strong.name: Male speech, man speaking
strong.description: Speech uttered by an adult male human.

strong.name: Cupboard open or close
strong.description: The sound of the door to a storage cabinet being opened or closed.

strong.name: Domestic animals, pets
strong.description: Sounds of animals kept in close proximity to humans for company, protection, and entertainment.

strong.name: Pig
strong.description: Sounds associated with the highly intelligent, very common, domesticated relative of the boar.

strong.name: Skateboard
strong.description: Sounds of a type of sports equipment consisting of a board mounted on two pairs of wheels. A skateboard is typically propelled by pushing with one foot while the other remains on the board, or by simply standing on the deck while on a downward slope and allowing gravity to propel the board and rider.

strong.name: Environmental noise
strong.description: The combined sounds of transport, industrial, and recreational activities.

strong.name: Rapping
strong.description: The sound of "spoken or chanted rhyming lyrics", serving the role of a vocal line in music but with normal speech intonation instead of a melodic line.

strong.name: Radio
strong.description: A sound that appears to have been produced by a radio receiver.

strong.name: Rail transport
strong.description: Sounds associated with wheeled vehicles running on rails (tracks).

strong.name: Run
strong.description: Move fast by using one's feet.

strong.name: Steam whistle
strong.description: The sound of a device used to produce sound with the aid of live steam, which acts as a vibrating system.

strong.name: Rodents, rats, mice
strong.description: Sounds associated with the small mammals of the order Rodentia, found in vast numbers on all continents except Antarctica.

strong.name: Rain
strong.description: The sound of droplets of liquid water that have condensed from atmospheric water vapor and then fallen under gravity.

strong.name: Ship
strong.description: The sound of a large buoyant watercraft, distinguished from boats based on size, shape, and cargo or passenger capacity.

strong.name: Steam
strong.description: Sounds caused by  water in the gas phase, which is formed when water boils.

strong.name: Mains hum
strong.description: A low, continuous tone caused by electromagnetic interference from the alternating current of the mains electricity. The fundamental frequency of this sound is usually 50 Hz or 60 Hz, depending on the local power-line frequency.

strong.name: Cap gun
strong.description: The sound of a toy gun that creates a loud sound simulating a gunshot and a puff of smoke when a small percussion cap is exploded.

strong.name: Snake
strong.description: Sounds associated with the elongated, legless, carnivorous reptiles of the suborder Serpentes.

strong.name: Sonar
strong.description: Sounds associated with underwater sensing via acoustic signals. A classic sonar sound involves reverberant reflections of an emitted tone pip.

strong.name: Wolf-whistling
strong.description: A two-toned whistle commonly made to show high interest or approval of something or someone (typically sexual).

strong.name: Sheep
strong.description: Sounds associated with the familiar quadrupedal, ruminant mammal typically kept as livestock.

strong.name: Single-lens reflex camera
strong.description: Sounds of camera that uses a mirror and prism system to permit the photographer to view through the lens and see exactly what will be captured.

strong.name: Sound reproduction
strong.description: A class for sounds that reveal the particular equipment used to capture or reproduce the sound.

strong.name: Television
strong.description: A sound that appears to have been produced by a television set.

strong.name: Telephone
strong.description: The sound of a telecommunications device that permits two or more users to conduct a conversation when they are too far apart to be heard directly.  This class covers sounds associated with the device itself, not voice that has been carried via the telephone network.

strong.name: Unmodified field recording
strong.description: A sound that appears to have been recorded in some specific environment, usually with the intention of capturing and representing that environment.

strong.name: Train
strong.description: The sound of one or more coupled vehicles running on a rail track to transport cargo or passengers, propelled by a separate locomotive or individual motors in each railroad car.

strong.name: Tools
strong.description: Sounds associated with any physical item that can be used to achieve a goal, especially if the item is not consumed in the process.

strong.name: Chorus effect
strong.description: The ensemble sound produced by an electronic effects unit which outputs simultaneous versions of the input source with small variations in pitch and timbre.

strong.name: Wheeze
strong.description: A continuous, coarse, whistling sound produced by obstruction of the respiratory airways during breathing.

strong.name: Tuning fork
strong.description: The sound of an acoustic resonator in the form of a two-pronged fork with the prongs formed from a U-shaped bar of elastic metal. It emits a pure musical tone and is frequently used as a standard of pitch to tune musical instruments.

strong.name: Shout
strong.description: Talk in a loud voice to deliberately command attention or overcome interfering sounds. Does not have the stronger emotional connotations of Yell or Scream.

strong.name: Slosh
strong.description: The sound of small waves of liquid held in a container breaking against the edges.

strong.name: Zing
strong.description: A brief high-pitched buzzing or humming sound.

strong.name: Fill (with liquid)
strong.description: The sound of a container being filled with liquid.

strong.name: Sizzle
strong.description: The sound of many small bubbles bursting, most often caused by fat vaporizing as it is heated.

strong.name: Throbbing
strong.description: A dull, continunous sound with a strong rhythmic modulation.

strong.name: Idling
strong.description: The sound of an engine (typically in an automobile) running without any load and at minimal RPM.

strong.name: Walk, footsteps
strong.description: The sound of feet or shoes contacting the ground in conventional human locomotion.

strong.name: Snap
strong.description: The sound of a thin and rigid element breaking suddenly and abruptly.

strong.name: Breaking
strong.description: The sound of a rigid object become separated into pieces or fragments.

strong.name: Chop
strong.description: The sound of cutting a solid material such as wood into smaller pieces by using an ax or other hacking tool.

strong.name: Biting
strong.description: Gripping or chewing off with the teeth and jaws.

strong.name: Rub
strong.description: The sound of two surfaces moving smoothly over each other with pressure but without excessive friction.

strong.name: Chirp, tweet
strong.description: A brief sound as made by a small bird.

strong.name: Rumble
strong.description: A loud, low-pitched, dull, continuous noise.

strong.name: Ding
strong.description: A high-pitched ringing sound, as of a small metal object being struck.

strong.name: Smash, crash
strong.description: The sound of a rigid structure violently breaking into many pieces.

strong.name: Buzz
strong.description: The sound of rapid vibration, commonly the wings of a flying insect.

strong.name: Wobble
strong.description: The sound of a structure shaking unsteadily back and forth, as in response to an impact.

strong.name: Splinter
strong.description: The sound of a rigid fibrous material, typically wood, breaking up into splinters or slivers.

strong.name: Crushing
strong.description: The sound of a brittle, rigid structure breaking into small pieces or catastrophically deforming.

strong.name: Sigh
strong.description: An utterance made by exhaling audibly.

strong.name: Chopping (food)
strong.description: The sound of cutting ingredients into pieces with a knife or similar blade tool.

strong.name: Telephone bell ringing
strong.description: The sound of a physical or synthesized electric bell ringing to signal an incoming telephone call.

strong.name: Alarm
strong.description: The sound of an automatic signal warning of danger.

strong.name: Sniff
strong.description: Inhale audibly through the nose.

strong.name: Trickle, dribble
strong.description: The sound of a liquid flowing slowly in an unsteady stream or drops.

strong.name: Bouncing
strong.description: The sound of an elastic, non-destructive collision in which one or both objects spring back. Depending on the situation, there may be multiple such collisions in a characteristic pattern, as of a ball bouncing.

strong.name: Pour
strong.description: The sound of liquid being transferred in a steady stream.

strong.name: Grind
strong.description: The sound of a substance being reduced to small pieces or particles by pounding or abrading, or the sound of two surfaces rubbing with high friction that suggests that one or both surfaces are being disintergrated.

strong.name: Pulse
strong.description: A sound that is modulated in short, regular bursts at approximately 1 Hz.  This class is not for heartbeat sounds, use /m/01jg02.

strong.name: Stir
strong.description: The sound of moving an implement through a fluid substance.

strong.name: Pump (liquid)
strong.description: The sound of a liquid being drawn or poured with a pump.

strong.name: Bang
strong.description: A brief and loud noise.

strong.name: Eruption
strong.description: The sound of a volcano violently ejecting ash and lava, or a similar event in which large volumes of material are explosively released.

strong.name: Flap
strong.description: The noisy sound of a flexible surface, such as a flag, moving back-and-forth in the air and optionally coming into contact with an adjacent hard surface.

strong.name: Pant
strong.description: Fast and noisy breathing, often associated with physical exertion.

strong.name: Crackle
strong.description: An irregular sequence of sharp sounds, as from sudden vaporization of liquids trapped in a burning solid, or from a collection of snapping noises.

strong.name: Bleat
strong.description: Communicative vocalization of sheep and goats.

strong.name: Snort
strong.description: The sound of a single, hard exhalation through the nose.

strong.name: Accelerating, revving, vroom
strong.description: The sound made by the engine of a vehicle undergoing acceleration, usually involving an increase in loudness and a rising pitch.

strong.name: Puff
strong.description: The sound of a gas, such as air, being blown forcefully in a short burst.

strong.name: Bellow
strong.description: A very loud utterance by a person that seems more animal than human.

strong.name: Neigh, whinny
strong.description: The characteristic communication sound made by a horse.

strong.name: Squeak
strong.description: A short, high-pitched noise without a sharp attack.

strong.name: Glass chink, clink
strong.description: A short light metallic sound.

strong.name: Howl (wind)
strong.description: A loud sustained noise caused by wind, resembling the cry of a hound.

strong.name: Screech
strong.description: A high-pitched noise with a rough quality resembling the cry of a human or other animal.

strong.name: Scratch
strong.description: The sound of a hard, sharp point of contact leaving a permanent groove in a hard surface.

strong.name: Clicking
strong.description: A short, pitchless, transient sound, as of a gentle impact between small hard objects.

strong.name: Tap
strong.description: The sound of a light collision between a rigid object and a rigid surface, for instance to deliberately attract attention.

strong.name: Tearing
strong.description: The sound of a flat or smooth surface separating abruptly.

strong.name: Quack
strong.description: The harsh communication sound made by a duck.

strong.name: Howl
strong.description: The long plaintive cry of a dog, wolf, or other canidae.

strong.name: Jingle, tinkle
strong.description: An irregular pattern of short metallic sounds, especially from small metal objects such as keys or coins shaking against each other.

strong.name: Hubbub, speech noise, speech babble
strong.description: Loud, disordered, unintelligible speech noise from many sources.

strong.name: Creak
strong.description: A high-pitched noise with a perceptible variation in pitch as a result of pressure being shifted or applied on a surface, most commonly on wood.

strong.name: Tick-tock
strong.description: A steady recurrent ticking sound as made by a clock.

strong.name: Tick
strong.description: A metallic tapping sound.

strong.name: Spray
strong.description: The sound of a liquid being transferred in a scatter or jet of droplets.

strong.name: Squish
strong.description: Sounds made by a liquid-saturated material being squeezed.

strong.name: Clatter
strong.description: An irregular rattling noise, often produced by rapid movement, consisting of a cluster of transient sounds.

strong.name: Rattle
strong.description: A rapid series of short loud sounds as of small hard items loose inside a container.

strong.name: Crowing, cock-a-doodle-doo
strong.description: The multi-syllable warning call made by a rooster (male chicken).

strong.name: Thump, thud
strong.description: A heavy dull sound, as made by impact of heavy objects with a relatively soft point of contact.

strong.name: Boom
strong.description: A deep prolonged loud noise.

strong.name: Meow
strong.description: The classic tonal communication sound made by cats.

strong.name: Crack
strong.description: Abrupt sounds of individual ruptures in a rigid substance under stress.

strong.name: Burst, pop
strong.description: The sound of an enclosure holding gas or liquid coming open suddenly and violently.

strong.name: Scrape
strong.description: The sound of a hard edge dragging across a surface.

strong.name: Shuffle
strong.description: Walk while dragging the feet, often indicating impaired mobility.

strong.name: Wail, moan
strong.description: A weak or soft emotional vocalization, possibly indicating pain, sadness, or pleasure.

strong.name: Ping
strong.description: A sharp high-pitched resonant sound with a clear decay.

strong.name: Honk
strong.description: The cry of a goose.

strong.name: Rustle
strong.description: A sound of light, thin objects, such as dried leaves, rubbing against one another.

strong.name: Plop
strong.description: The sound of a small object dropping into a liquid without a splash.

strong.name: Whimper
strong.description: A plaintive, whining vocalization with some abrupt changes in loudness.

strong.name: Truck
strong.description: Sounds of large motor vehicles designed to transport cargo on roads.

strong.name: Raindrop
strong.description: A sound clearly attributable to a single drop of rain.

strong.name: Patter
strong.description: A quick succession of light rapid sounds, usually suggesting the locomotion of small animals.

strong.name: Grunt
strong.description: A short low gruff noise, resembling the sound made by animals such as pigs. Specifically refers to humans.

strong.name: Knock
strong.description: A sharp noise of a rigid surface being struck, usually without damage and deliberately, most often with the knuckles of the hand.

strong.name: Caw
strong.description: The relatively harsh sound made by corvine birds.

strong.name: Drip
strong.description: The sound of liquid falling in drops.

strong.name: Giggle
strong.description: A foolish or nervous laugh.

strong.name: Ding-dong
strong.description: A multi-tone chime made by a doorbell.

strong.name: Caterwaul
strong.description: The yowling sound made by a cat in heat.

strong.name: Coo
strong.description: The sound made by a pigeon or dove.

strong.name: Hoot
strong.description: The loud raucous cry of an owl.

strong.name: Yip
strong.description: A sharp high-pitched bark or cry, typically from a miniature dog.

strong.name: Whip
strong.description: The sound of whipping, i.e., the greatly accelerated motion of the tip of a flexible structure, as the result of concentrated angular momentum.

strong.name: Bow-wow
strong.description: Dog communication sound that is more tonal and less abrupt than a classic bark.

strong.name: Hum
strong.description: A continuous, dull tone.

strong.name: Whack, thwack
strong.description: The sound of a partially rigid object forcefully striking another object, which may be preceded by the sound of the rapid, driven motion of one object (as of a baseball bat hitting a ball).

strong.name: Static
strong.description: A crackling or hissing noise caused by electrical interference.

strong.name: Chuckle, chortle
strong.description: Laugh quietly or with restraint.

strong.name: Hiss
strong.description: A fricative sound, such as from a cat giving warning, or an audience indicating disapproval.

strong.name: Slam
strong.description: The sound of a door or other hinged cover being closed violently.

strong.name: Glass shatter
strong.description: The sound of a brittle rigid substance rapidly breaking into many pieces.

strong.name: Moo
strong.description: The classic communication sound made by a cow or bull.

strong.name: Whoosh, swoosh, swish
strong.description: A sibilant sound caused by a rigid object sweeping through the air.

strong.name: Thunk
strong.description: A partly dull hollow sound with a damped resonance.

strong.name: Splash, splatter
strong.description: The sound of a liquid colliding with a hard surface.

strong.name: Clang
strong.description: A loud, resonant, discordant noise, as of a large and partly hollow metal structure begin struck.

strong.name: Clip-clop
strong.description: The sound of a horse's hoofs hitting on a hard surface.

strong.name: Whoop
strong.description: A loud hooting cry of exultation or excitement.

strong.name: Clickety-clack
strong.description: The sound of fast and rhythmic clicking of machinery, such as keystrokes on a typewriter or steel wheels running on tracks.  Does not include the sound of horses feet (use /m/07rv9rh).

strong.name: Slap, smack
strong.description: The sharp sound of a flat object striking another (e.g., an open hand hitting a face).

strong.name: Squeal
strong.description: A short, high-pitched tone without a sharp attack and with a perceptible variation in pitch.

strong.name: Snicker
strong.description: A disrespectful laugh.

strong.name: Gasp
strong.description: A short labored intake of breath with the mouth open. Often indicates shock or surprise.

strong.name: Crunch
strong.description: The sound of a brittle substance being crushed.

strong.name: Groan
strong.description: An utterance expressing pain or disapproval. Specifically refers to humans.

strong.name: Whir
strong.description: A quiet sound of a small object, typically mechanical, in rapid, cyclic motion.

strong.name: Roll
strong.description: The sound of an object moving by turning over or rotating.

strong.name: Belly laugh
strong.description: Very loud and abrupt laughter that encompasses much of the body.

strong.name: Yell
strong.description: Utter or declare in a very loud voice that seems excessive or involuntary, or that is deliberately startling in order to command attention, as distinct from the pragmatically raised voice of Shout.

strong.name: Croak
strong.description: The harsh hoarse utterance of a frog.

strong.name: Cluck
strong.description: The soft, low-pitched, and repetitive sound made by chickens.

strong.name: Gobble
strong.description: The characteristic sound made by a turkey cock.

strong.name: Gurgling, bubbling
strong.description: The bubbling sound of water flowing through a narrow constriction, such as from a bottle with a narrow neck.

strong.name: Squawk
strong.description: Abrasive, unpleasant sharp sound produced by a bird.

strong.name: Cacophony
strong.description: A loud, confusing, disagreeable sound, such as many voices shouting simultaneously.

strong.name: Vehicle
strong.description: Sounds of mobile machines that transport people or cargo.

strong.name: Writing
strong.description: The sound of inscribing signs and symbols, most often by using a purpose-made hand-held device, such as a pen or pencil, directly upon paper or similar media.

strong.name: Water
strong.description: Sounds caused by motion of liquid water.

strong.name: Wood
strong.description: Sounds associated with the porous and fibrous structural tissue found in the stems and roots of trees, and other woody plants.

strong.name: Dental drill, dentist's drill
strong.description: The sound of a small, high-speed drill used during dental procedures, usually to remove decay and shape tooth structure prior to the insertion of a filling or crown.

strong.name: Vehicle horn, car horn, honking, toot
strong.description: The sound of a motor vehicle accessory whose purpose is to provide an audible alert of the vehicle's presence.

strong.name: Gargling
strong.description: Air from the lungs bubbling through a liquid in the mouth.

strong.name: Background noise
strong.description: Sounds present alongside a sound of interest but typically weaker in energy and generally not of interest.

strong.name: Noise
strong.description: A sound that has no perceptible structure and that typically interferes with the perception of more interesting or important sounds.

strong.name: Chicken, rooster
strong.description: Sounds of the very common and widespread domesticated fowl, raised for its eggs and meat.

strong.name: Helicopter
strong.description: Sounds of a type of rotorcraft in which lift and thrust are supplied by rotors. This allows the helicopter to take off and land vertically, to hover, and to fly forward, backward, and laterally.

strong.name: Tape hiss
strong.description: A high frequency noise present on analog magnetic tape recordings caused by the size of the magnetic particles used to make the tape.

strong.name: Owl
strong.description: Sounds associated with the mostly solitary and nocturnal carnivorous birds from the order Strigiformes.

strong.name: Ducks, geese, waterfowl
strong.description: Sounds associated with this collection of waterfowl species.

strong.name: Mosquito
strong.description: Sounds associated with these small, midge-like flies whose tube-like mouth parts pierce the hosts' skin to consume blood.

strong.name: Respiratory sounds
strong.description: Sounds generated by the movement of air through the respiratory system (nose, mouth, trachea, and lungs).

strong.name: Human voice
strong.description: The human voice consists of sound made by a human being using the vocal folds for talking, singing, laughing, crying, screaming, etc. The human voice is specifically a part of human sound production in which the vocal folds are the primary sound source.

strong.name: Frog
strong.description: Sounds associated with the short-bodied, tailless amphibians composing the order Anura.

strong.name: Speech
strong.description: Speech is the vocalized form of human communication, created out of the phonetic combination of a limited set of vowel and consonant speech sound units.

strong.name: Cricket
strong.description: Sounds associated with these relatives of grasshoppers characterized by enlarged hind legs, providing power for jumping. Crickets are mainly nocturnal, and are best known for the loud, persistent, chirping song of males trying to attract females.

strong.name: Artillery fire
strong.description: The sound of large military weapons built to fire munitions far beyond the range and power of infantry's small arms.

strong.name: Power tool
strong.description: Sounds of tools that employ a power source other than the manual labor used with hand tools. The most common types of power tools use electric motors.

strong.name: Electronic tuner
strong.description: Sounds produced by an electronic device whose purpose is to aid in the tuning of musical instruments.

strong.name: Human locomotion
strong.description: Sounds resulting from human body actions involved in changing location.

strong.name: Speech synthesizer
strong.description: Artificially-produced human speech.

strong.name: Dog
strong.description: Any sounds coming from the familiar domesticated canid which has been selectively bred over millennia for companionship, protection, as well as for superior sensory capabilities, and other useful behaviors.

strong.name: Traffic noise, roadway noise
strong.description: The combined sounds of many motor vehicles traveling on roads.

strong.name: Sound effect
strong.description: An artificially created or enhanced sound used to emphasize artistic or other content of films, television shows, live performances, animation, video games, music, or other media.

strong.name: Typewriter
strong.description: Sounds of a mechanical or electromechanical machine for printing characters by means of keyboard-operated types striking a ribbon to transfer ink or carbon impressions onto paper.

strong.name: Fire alarm
strong.description: Sounds of a system designed to warn people when smoke, fire, carbon monoxide or other emergencies are present. Alarms can be either motorized bells or wall-mountable sounders or horns.

strong.name: Roaring cats (lions, tigers)
strong.description: Sounds associated with the larger and more ferocious wild relatives of cats.

strong.name: Livestock, farm animals, working animals
strong.description: Sound made by animals associated with farms and agriculture.

strong.name: White noise, pink noise
strong.description: A random, unstructured sound in which the value at any moment provides no information about the value at any other moment. White noise has equal energy in all frequency bands.

strong.name: Fixed-wing aircraft, airplane
strong.description: Sounds of an aircraft capable of flight using wings that generate lift caused by the vehicle's forward airspeed and the shape of the wings.

strong.name: Vacuum cleaner
strong.description: The sound of a device that uses an air pump to create a partial vacuum to suck up dust and dirt, usually from floors and other surfaces such as upholstery and draperies.

strong.name: Civil defense siren
strong.description: The sound of a siren used to provide emergency population warning of approaching danger such as hurricanes, earthquakes, or military attacks.

strong.name: Human sounds
strong.description: Sounds produced by the human body through the actions of the individual.

strong.name: Arrow
strong.description: Sounds of a shafted projectile that is shot with a bow.

strong.name: Throat clearing
strong.description: Forced exhalation through a partially-closed glottis to disrupt built-up mucus, or used as a social signal to draw attention to one's presence.

strong.name: Boiling
strong.description: The sound of a liquid that is reaching the temperature at which it transitions to a vapor, resulting in bubbles emerging at the surface.

strong.name: Camera
strong.description: Sounds of mechanical or electronic instruments that employ optics to record or capture images.

strong.name: Frying (food)
strong.description: The sound of cooking food in oil or another fat.

strong.name: Chime
strong.description: The sound of a musical instrument consisting of multiple tuned bells, usually rung by an automated mechanism to produce a short, characteristic tone or melody.

strong.name: Donkey, ass
strong.description: Sounds associated with the domesticated working animal that is a smaller member of the horse family.

strong.name: Wildfire
strong.description: Sounds of an uncontrolled fire in an area of combustible vegetation that occurs in the countryside.

strong.name: Drawer open or close
strong.description: The sound of the opening or closing of a box-shaped container that fits into a piece of furniture in such a way that it can be drawn out horizontally to reach its contents.

strong.name: Microwave oven
strong.description: Sounds made by a kitchen appliance that heats food by exposing it to microwave radiation, including the noise of the fan, rotation mechanism, and microwave source, as well as the alert sound used to indicate that cooking is complete.

strong.name: Distortion
strong.description: A sound that has been modified in a nonlinear fashion, usually in electronic equipment, to introduce sound correlated with the original signal. In many cases, notably with amplified electric musical instruments, distortion is introduced as an effect by increasing the gain and clipping the source signal.

strong.name: Fireworks
strong.description: Sounds of a class of low explosive pyrotechnic devices used for aesthetic and entertainment purposes.

strong.name: Growling
strong.description: A low, guttural vocalization produced by animals as a warning, a sign of aggression, or to express anger.

strong.name: Air brake
strong.description: Sounds of a vehicle braking system in which compressed air is used to transmit force to the brake pads on the wheels. The pneumatic system makes an abrupt hissing sound when the pressure is released by venting the air.

strong.name: Bicycle bell
strong.description: The sound of a percussive signaling instrument mounted on a bicycle for warning pedestrians and other cyclists.

strong.name: Pigeon, dove
strong.description: Sounds associated with these species of birds having short necks and short, slender bills.

strong.name: Fly, housefly
strong.description: Sounds associated with these insects of the order Diptera, which use only a single pair of wings to fly.

strong.name: Tire squeal, skidding
strong.description: The high-pitched sound of a rubber vehicle tire sliding over a road surface when the torque applied to the wheel (to either accelerate or decelerate) exceeds the maximum frictional force that can be supported.

strong.name: Chirp tone
strong.description: A tone whose frequency increases or decreases with time.

strong.name: Microphone
strong.description: Sounds whose origin lie with the microphone used in the recording, rather than the external sound source that was intended to be recorded.

strong.name: Sailboat, sailing ship
strong.description: Sounds of a boat (large or small) propelled partly or entirely by sails.

strong.name: Waterfall
strong.description: The sound of water flowing over a vertical drop or a series of drops in the course of a stream or river.

strong.name: Stream, river
strong.description: Sounds of a body of water with a current, confined within a bed and banks.

strong.name: Thunderstorm
strong.description: The sound of a storm characterized by the presence of lightning and its acoustic effect on the Earth's atmosphere, known as thunder.

strong.name: Animal
strong.description: All sound produced by the bodies and actions of nonhuman animals.

strong.name: Car
strong.description: Sounds of a self-powered motor vehicle with usually four wheels used for transportation of one to eight people, designed to run primarily on roads.

strong.name: Aircraft
strong.description: Sound of vehicles that fly by gaining support from the air.

strong.name: Hands
strong.description: Sounds originating primarily from the hands and fingers of humans.

strong.name: Choir
strong.description: A musical ensemble of singers.

strong.name: Whistle
strong.description: The sound of an instrument that produces sound from a stream of forced air.

strong.name: Clapping
strong.description: A percussive sound made by a human striking together the palms of their two hands, often quickly and repeatedly to express appreciation or approval. This category is to be used for distinct claps by a single person; for a group of people clapping together, use Applause.

strong.name: Gears
strong.description: Sounds of rotating machine parts having cut teeth, or cogs, which mesh with other toothed parts to transmit torque.

strong.name: Sewing machine
strong.description: Sounds of a machine used to stitch fabric and other materials together with thread.

strong.name: Race car, auto racing
strong.description: The sound of one or more motor vehicles engaged in a competition to complete a course as quickly as possible. Specialized race cars include many modifications, often making them much louder than common street vehicles.

strong.name: Breathing
strong.description: Air being moved in and out of the lungs in order to sustain life.

strong.name: Power saw, circular saw, table saw
Thunder
strong.description: The sound caused by lightning. Depending on the distance and nature of the lightning, thunder can range from a sharp, loud crack to a long, low rumble.

strong.name: Child speech, kid speaking
strong.description: Speech uttered by a human child, i.e. a human whose voice does not yet resemble that of an adult.

strong.name: Velcro, hook and loop fastener
strong.description: Sounds of fasteners typically consisting of two lineal fabric strips, one featuring tiny hooks, the second consisting of even smaller and "hairier" loops.

strong.name: Baby laughter
strong.description: Laughter that is produced by a baby or infant.

strong.name: Baby cry, infant cry
strong.description: The sound of a young child crying or bawling.

strong.name: Male singing
strong.description: Singing produced by an adult human male.

strong.name: Female singing
strong.description: Singing produced by an adult human female.

strong.name: Child singing
strong.description: Singing produced by a young human whose voice has not yet reached its adult state.

strong.name: Synthetic singing
strong.description: Singing-like sounds produced by artificial means, such as an electronic synthesizer.  Does not include pre-recorded sounds that originate in a human voice.

strong.name: Human group actions
strong.description: Sounds produced by groups of humans rather than individuals.

strong.name: Children playing
strong.description: The sound of children at play, including any of vocalization or the sounds of their activities.

strong.name: Oink
strong.description: Common vocalization sound associated with pigs.

strong.name: Rain on surface
strong.description: Steady sound of many rain drops striking a surface such as a roof or window.

strong.name: Train wheels squealing
strong.description: The high-pitched tones caused by steel train wheels rubbing against rails, for instance when traversing a tight bend or when braking.

strong.name: Non-motorized land vehicle
strong.description: Sounds of human-powered vehicles used on roads or elsewhere on land.

strong.name: Light engine (high frequency)
strong.description: The sound of a small engine such as a toy car, sewing machine, or moped.

strong.name: Medium engine (mid frequency)
strong.description: The sound of a moderately-sized engine such as that which powers a motorcycle, sedan, or small truck.

strong.name: Heavy engine (low frequency)
strong.description: The sound of a large, heavy-duty internal combustion engine, such as that which powers a large truck, locomotive, or ship.  Jet engines, steam engines, rocket engines etc. are excluded.

strong.name: Mechanisms
strong.description: Sounds that originate from human-created machinery and devices.

strong.name: Gush
strong.description: The sound of a liquid coming out of a pipe or other opening rapidly and in large volumes.

strong.name: Sound equipment
strong.description: Sounds that suggest the involvement of electronic audio processing equipment.

strong.name: Wind noise (microphone)
strong.description: The noise produced when a strong air current passes over a microphone, causing large amplitude local turbulence, normally recorded as mechanical clipping as the microphone element exceeds its limits of linearity.

strong.name: Source-ambiguous sounds
strong.description: Portmanteau class for sounds that do not immediately suggest specific source objects, but which are more likely to be perceived and described according to their acoustic properties.

strong.name: Generic impact sounds
strong.description: Sounds of impacts or collisions preferentially described by their acoustic properties, rather than by immediately referring to their assumed source object(s).

strong.name: Clunk
strong.description: A predominantly low-frequency impact noise that starts with a cleaner, high-frequency click, suggesting the contact of rigid surfaces (as of a car door closing).

strong.name: Surface contact
strong.description: Sounds produced by a more extended interaction between two objects or surfaces instead of a collision or bounce.

strong.name: Deformable shell
strong.description: Sounds that are associated with shells, rigid sheets, or other predominantly two-dimensional surfaces.

strong.name: Crumpling, crinkling
strong.description: The sound of a rigid but flexible sheet, such as paper or aluminum, buckling into a smaller volume.

strong.name: Fizz
strong.description: The sound of the popping of many small bubbles, most often as gas is released from solution, such as in a carbonated beverage.

strong.name: Boing
strong.description: A bouncing or spring-like sound with a tonal component that sweeps upwards.

strong.name: Other sourceless
strong.description: A class for sound categories not represented by other classes that are peceived by their sound instead of their source.

strong.name: Channel, environment and background
strong.description: A class for sound categories that suggest information about attributes other than the foreground or target objects.

strong.name: Inside, small room
strong.description: Sounds that appear to have been recorded within a small room, such as one that can accommodate no more than 15 people.

strong.name: Inside, large room or hall
strong.description: Sounds that appear to have been recorded in a large room or hall, often with clearly perceptible reverberation.

strong.name: Inside, public space
strong.description: Sounds that appear to have been recorded in a public space such as store, restaurant, or travel terminus, often characterized by both reverberation and continuous background noise.

strong.name: Outside, urban or manmade
strong.description: Sounds that appear to have been recorded outdoors in a human-constructed environment.

strong.name: Outside, rural or natural
strong.description: Sounds that appear to have been recorded outdoors in a natural, non-manmade environment.

strong.name: Engine starting
strong.description: The sound of an engine starting from rest, which may involve a specific starter mechanism (as in a standard car).

strong.name: Specific impact sounds
strong.description: Transient contact sounds that are strongly suggestive of the particular objects involved in the collision.

strong.name: Car passing by
strong.description: The sound of a motorized vehicle as it passes by a listener close to the vehicle's path. The sound may include engine and tire noise and will typically involve a clear build-up and/or decay of intensity as the vehicle approaches and retreats, as well as possible Doppler shift.

strong.name: Children shouting
strong.description: The boisterous vocalizations of a group of children, for instance in a playground.

strong.name: Whimper (dog)
strong.description: Muted dog vocalization indicating submission, fear, or pain.

strong.name: Snort (horse)
strong.description: The sound of a rapid exhale through a horse's nose.
